note: Seeded 2026-09-22. SCOPE: Peruvian cooking in London, across all three of the forms the city actually sells it in - Nikkei (Japanese-Peruvian), criollo home cooking, and ceviche-and-pisco bar rooms. Nikkei rooms that sit in the Japanese corpus are NOT re-counted here: Sushisamba's japanese-corpus citations stay in that topic (trap 7). Every URL below was read in this pass. NO CURRENT JUDGED AWARD EXISTS FOR THIS TOPIC: the National Restaurant Awards 2025 top 100 carries no Peruvian restaurant, and Michelin's only Peruvian star in Greater London - Lima Fitzrovia - ran from the 2014 guide to the 2018. That raises the social floor to three voices; three YouTube creators are recorded. TIER E IS EMPTY: Reddit answers old.reddit.com, the JSON API, redlib mirrors and safereddit with an interstitial or a 403 in this environment, and TikTok serves a login wall, so no community thread could be read. CLOSURES ESTABLISHED IN THIS PASS: Pachamama (the group's own site now offers zephyr, Bottarga, Nina and Lagana instead, and says Pachamama will be back one day soon) and Chicama (its operator states the King's Road restaurant's last service was 15 September; the year is not stated). STATUS UNKNOWN AND DELIBERATELY OMITTED FROM THE GUIDE: Ceviche, Andina, MOMMI and Cuzco, none of which this pass can positively establish as trading. See openVenueQuestions in data/topics/peruvian.json.

sources.name: Time Out - London's best Peruvian restaurants

quotes.Lima: #1 of 20. 'A contemporary Peruvian restaurant with locations in Fitzrovia and Shoreditch. The former is our favourite... headed by chef Diego Recarte.' Lunch deal noon-3pm weekdays, £27 for a starter and main, £5 pisco sours.
quotes.Llama Inn: #2 of 20. 'Colourful, modern Peruvian on The Hoxton Shoreditch hotel rooftop... The menu leans towards contemporary Chifa, but you'll find some Nikkei treasures, too.' £1 oyster deal at Monday lunch.
quotes.Darkest Peru: #3 of 20. 'London's first Peruvian cafe' - run by Pedro Tello, a Peruvian architect-turned-foodie. Salchicha sandwich, Lomito sandwich. Hosts monthly BYOB private dining nights.
quotes.Tierra Peru: #4 of 20. 'A Peruvian food stall turned Islington brick-and-mortar on Essex Road... A favourite among London-based Peruvians.' Started as a food stall in Camden.
quotes.Jarana Peruvian Restaurant & Pisco Bar: #5 of 20. 'A Fulham-based restaurant and pisco bar with the best pollo a la brasa.' The chicken is roasted in a custom rig delivered from Peru. Menu changes almost weekly.
quotes.Ayllu: #6 of 20. 'An intimate Paddington restaurant' with a Nikkei-forward menu - oysters with truffle and leche de tigre, tuna tataki tiraditos.
quotes.Señor Ceviche: #7 of 20. 'Affordable Nikkei in Soho.' Monday deal: any ceviche and any pisco sour for £6 each.
quotes.Maka: #8 of 20. 'A south London stunner' on the Oval end of Brixton Road. Acevichado chicken wings glazed in a cross between leche de tigre and aioli; causa Limeña.
quotes.Chan Chan: #9 of 20. 'A food stall in Peckham's Rye Lane Market with all the classics and beyond,' run by Carlos Medina and Carla. Parihuela at weekends.
quotes.Lima Limón: #10 of 20. 'A small Peruvian kitchen in Brixton that's pretty in pink.' Jalea; pulpo a la brasa rather than pollo a la brasa; picarones.
quotes.El Alquimista: #11 of 20. 'Sophisticated Peruvian plates served a la Francaise' from Peru-born chef Walter Pineda in Greenwich. Pichón anticuchos. Two-course pre-theatre menu £39 Tue-Fri 5-6.30pm.
quotes.Mr LoBo: #12 of 20. 'A cosy restaurant in Angel filled with Peruvian art.' Ox heart anticuchos; Chicha Sour.
quotes.Chakana: #13 of 20. 'A south Hackney spot dedicated to Peru's flagship ingredients. In charge is Peruvian native and Michelin-starred chef Robert Ortiz.' Crab causa; lucuma tiramisu; Peruvian Sunday roast.
quotes.Sabor Peruano: #14 of 20. 'Casual, cool and traditional Peruvian' with a Chifa-based menu at Elephant & Castle. Lomo saltado; arroz chaufa; mazamorra morada.
quotes.Bamboo Mat: #15 of 20. 'A Nikkei-focused, neon-lit dining space near Stratford station', opened in Leyton before moving to East Village in 2023.
quotes.Fan: #16 of 20. ‘Neo-Nikkei’ in Notting Hill. Nigiri with aji-amarillo or pachikay. £120 signature tasting menu, £39 day menu.
quotes.Crudo: #17 of 20. 'One of London's few stand-alone ceviche spots', opened by Maria and Carlos in Seven Dials.
quotes.Coya Mayfair: #18 of 20. 'Peruvian plates in an extravagant setting'... 'You go to Coya when you want to be seen.'
quotes.Chotto Matte: #19 of 20. 'An international chain devoted to all-things Nikkei', six global locations.
quotes.Sushisamba: #20 of 20. 'Might not be the most authentic or traditional, but it's a hell of a lot of fun.' Peruvian-Brazilian-Japanese, skewing Japanese.

sources.note: Ranked 1-20, by Daniela Toporek, published 21 August 2026. The only source in this pass that reaches Elephant & Castle, Peckham, Brixton, Greenwich and Stratford. Every entry carries an address, opening hours and a price range, which is why this pass treats it as the currency check on the whole set.

sources.name: The Infatuation - The Best Peruvian Restaurants In London

quotes.Sabor Peruano: 'Outside it's a canteen, but inside it gives 1960s banquet wedding... should be close to the top of your list in terms of Peruvian restaurants in London for three reasons: it's great-value, has traditional cooking, and it closes before 10pm.'
quotes.Tierra Peru: 'At Tierra Peru, it's impossible not to smile... The family-run Peruvian spot in Islington can make a Wednesday night feel like a weekend.' Chef recommends cordero huanuqueño and picante chalaco.
quotes.Llama Inn: 'Llama Inn came to London via New York and has made its home on the roof of The Hoxton hotel in Shoreditch... The menu's glossary, which explains the likes of aji rocoto, huacatay, and other Peruvian ingredients, partly shows the seriousness of the food.'
quotes.Pachamama East: PAGE FLAGS IT: 'This spot is Permanently Closed.' 73 Great Eastern Street, EC2A 3HR.

sources.name: The Nudge - The Best Peruvian Restaurants in London

quotes.Lima London: 'Lima set an unfair standard for the other Peruvian restaurants in London when it arrived on the scene, bagging a Michelin star in 2014 (the first Peruvian restaurant in Europe to do so)... owner-brothers Gabriel and Jose-Luis Gonzalez... the opening of Lima Shoreditch.'
quotes.Lima Cantina: 'Set in an old stained glass workshop, Lima Fitzrovia's sibling offers a window into one very specific part of Peruvian cuisine: rotisserie chicken. The restaurant's proudly home to London's only rotombo oven.' 14 Garrick Street, WC2E 9BJ - the address other sources give as Floral by LIMA.
quotes.Señor Ceviche: 'Ten years ago, London was blessed with a South American pop-up called Don Ceviche. It was chef and owner Harry Edmeades' way of getting a read on his renditions of Peru's national dish.'
quotes.Ceviche: 17 Frith Street, W1D 4RG. 'Modelled off Lima's artsy Barranco neighbourhood.'

sources.note: Published 18 October 2024, last modified 8 April 2026. Written by Rupert Hohwieler.

quotes.Lima: 'Lima Fitzrovia, fresh from a refurb and a menu revamp, is a different proposition to its previous, Michelin-star holding incarnation.'
quotes.The Llama Inn: 'The original Llama Inn opened in the Big Apple in 2015.' Lomo saltado served over an okonomiyaki-style pancake, £56. Speedy Lunch two courses £28, three for £33.

quotes.Lima Fitzrovia: One Michelin star in the 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017 and 2018 guides; no star from the 2019 guide onward. The only Peruvian restaurant ever starred in Greater London.

sources.note: guide.michelin.com answers the fetcher with a bot wall (HTTP 202, empty body), so the sanctioned substitute in data/sources.json was used. STARS ONLY - it cannot surface a Bib Gourmand.
